title: BATS density 26.5 AOU rose in spring and autumn without a larger warm-season increment between 1989-1998 and 2016-2025
abstract: We test whether the BATS oxygen deficit on potential-density anomaly 26.5 kg/m3 grows during the current warm season. We compare spring and autumn in the same sampled years, using BATS bottle data version 10. From 1989-1998 to 2016-2025, March-April apparent oxygen utilization (AOU) rose 10.87 umol/kg and September-October AOU rose 10.47. The autumn-minus-spring contrast changed by -0.40, with a 95 percent year-bootstrap interval of -3.15 to +2.60. Block resampling, other seasons, complete-month coverage and cubic interpolation retain this pattern. The deficit is already present in spring. Extra loss after spring with a fixed spring state cannot explain the autumn shift. This does not exclude respiration over many years, transport, mixing, or winter changes and does not identify an outcrop cause. The strict interpolation test has only two early and one late paired years and cannot estimate a change. Main results require wider bottle brackets. Code, aggregate evidence, exact source provenance and retrieval instructions are supplied.
